title: Device Handling: CPU, GPU & Multi‑GPU 🖥️
description: Move models between devices, handle GPU mapping, and use DataParallel.

slides.title: Moving Models Across Devices 🔄
slides.content:
# CPU ↔ GPU

A model's parameters live on a specific device. To move:
```python
model.to('cuda')   # move to GPU
model.to('cpu')    # move back to CPU
```
This affects all parameters and buffers (like BatchNorm running means).

slides.title: Device‑Agnostic Training
slides.content: Define a device variable and move model/data accordingly.
slides.codeSnippet:
device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
model = nn.Linear(10, 2).to(device)
x = torch.randn(5, 10).to(device)
out = model(x)
print(out.device)  # cuda:0 or cpu

quizData.question: What happens if you run a model on GPU with a CPU input tensor?

options.text: It automatically moves the input to GPU
It raises a RuntimeError due to device mismatch

quizData.explanation: All tensors in an operation must be on the same device.

slides.title: Multi‑GPU: DataParallel 🎛️
slides.content:
## Splitting Batches Across GPUs

`nn.DataParallel` replicates the model on multiple GPUs, splits each batch, and gathers results. Simplest way to use multiple GPUs:

```python
model = nn.DataParallel(model)
```
Now `model` can take input on any GPU; it distributes automatically.

slides.title: Using DataParallel
slides.content: Wrap a model and run on multiple GPUs (if available).
slides.codeSnippet:
device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
model = nn.Linear(10, 2).to(device)
if torch.cuda.device_count() > 1:
    model = nn.DataParallel(model)
x = torch.randn(64, 10).to(device)
out = model(x)
print(out.shape)

quizData.question: What does `nn.DataParallel` do?

options.text: Trains different models on each GPU
Replicates the model on each GPU and splits the batch to run in parallel

quizData.explanation: Data parallelism distributes the batch across GPUs, each running a copy of the model.

slides.title: Saving and Loading with Devices 📂
slides.content:
## Device‑Safe State Dicts

Saving a GPU model's state_dict and loading on CPU:
```python
torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'weights.pth')
model_cpu = ModelClass()
model_cpu.load_state_dict(torch.load('weights.pth', map_location='cpu'))
```
`map_location` remaps storage.

slides.title: Loading GPU Weights on CPU
slides.content: Remap a CUDA checkpoint to CPU.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Saved from GPU:
# torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'gpu_model.pth')

# Load on CPU
model = nn.Linear(10, 2)
state_dict = torch.load('gpu_model.pth', map_location='cpu')
model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
print('Model loaded on CPU')

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## For Multi‑GPU: Remove module. Prefix

When loading a DataParallel‑saved state_dict, keys have 'module.' prefix. Strip them with:
```python
from collections import OrderedDict
new_state = OrderedDict()
for k, v in state_dict.items():
    new_state[k.replace('module.', '')] = v
```
